**Triggers only on INSERT/UPDATE.** Existing rows stay plaintext until backfill (see above). The security review may flag this - backfill before going live.

**Key persistence.** If ENCRYPTION_KEY isn't in env.yaml or the env, the framework auto-generates one ONCE and persists it (env.yaml; on the hosted platform it is stored with the instance's environment, so every restart resolves the same key). Explicitly setting `benmore env set ENCRYPTION_KEY=<64-hex> --env prod` BEFORE writing encrypted data is still the most predictable path.

**Rotating on the platform.** Use `rotate_encryption_key` (owner): it picks or takes the new key and, once the app has re-encrypted, saves it to the instance's environment, which is what the next start loads. In a hosted app the app's own `/api/_internal/encryption/rotate` refuses a confirmed rotation that does not come through that tool (dry runs work), because a key the platform did not save would be gone at the next restart. CLI: `benmore rotate-key <app> --as <admin-email> [--new-key <string>] [--confirm] [--env dev|prod]` is a dry run (its answer carries the app's `rows_that_would_rotate`) until `--confirm`; `--new-key` supplies the new key's source string (at least 32 characters), and without it a key is generated.

**Decryption failure is masked, never leaked**. A value that looks encrypted but can't be decrypted under the owning database key comes back as `[unavailable: decryption failed]` instead of the raw `enc:v1:…` string, with a throttled server log line. If you see that mask, the active key doesn't match the key that wrote the data (rotated env.yaml? ciphertext copied from another environment?) - fix the key or re-write the data. An update that sends the mask back to an encrypted field is ignored and named in X-Ignored-Fields (see masked_echo), so an edit form that echoes the row does not overwrite it.

**OAuth tokens.** The framework uses benmore_encrypt internally for the _benmore_oauth_tokens table even when encrypted.yaml is empty - so the AES key matters for OAuth integrity, not just user-declared fields.
**Audit protection.** The audit log re-encrypts configured sensitive fields, including numeric values and old-value deltas, with the owning app key. Custom audit SQL must provide its own protection.

**Queued hook and webhook jobs**. The row a hook or webhook-subscription job carries has its encrypted.yaml columns and `old_` deltas sealed in `_benmore_jobs.payload` and opened at delivery, so hooks and subscribers receive the plain row. Key rotation re-seals jobs that can still run (pending, running, failed); completed jobs keep the old key's ciphertext. Jobs queued by an older runtime still deliver. Event flows, `run: enqueue` and async flow payloads are not sealed.

**Idempotent create responses**. A create with `X-Idempotency-Key` on a table with encrypted fields stores the response it answered (decrypted for that caller) sealed in `_benmore_idempotency` and opens it for a retry; key rotation re-seals the entries still inside the 24h window. See api({at:'idempotency'}).

**Auto-CRUD reads AND the POST-create response are decrypted + masked**. A POST returns the full new row already decrypted (owner/admin) or masked (others) - you do NOT need to re-fetch by id after creating to get plaintext. (PATCH returns just {status:'updated'}, no row.) Custom flow SQL results are decrypted with the app key; custom flows must apply their own authorization and field masking before returning results.

**A literal that starts `enc:v1:` or `enc:v2:` is data, not ciphertext.** The trigger seals any value that is not decryptable ciphertext for that same table and column, so seed SQL holding such a literal is encrypted like any other text and reads back unchanged. Only authentic ciphertext for the same field (key rotation, a restore of this app's own rows) is left as it is.
